chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abī Ayyūb, from Muʿādh ibn Kathīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“When a man enters the mosque while he is not following his companion, and there remains for the Imam one verse or two verses, and he fears that if he gives the adhan and iqamah the Imam will bow, then let him say: ‘Qad qāmati al-salāh, qad qāmati al-salāh, Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar, lā ilāha illā Allāh,’ and let him enter into the salat (prayer).”

key_terms.آيَةٌ: a verse of recitation remaining in the prayer
key_terms.أَذَّنَ: gave the adhan, the call to prayer
key_terms.أَقَامَ: gave the iqamah, the commencement call for prayer
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ ٱلصَّلَاةُ: the phrase of iqamah indicating that the salat (prayer) has begun
key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ: there is no god but Allah, the declaration of divine unity
key_terms.ٱللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Allah is greatest, a formula of magnification in worship
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader in the congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱلْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, the place entered for congregational worship

ai.seo_question: What should a person say if he enters the mosque late and fears missing the Imam’s ruku' during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who enters the mosque late and fears missing the congregational prayer if he performs the full adhan and iqamah. In such a case, he suffices with a shortened iqamah formula and then joins the salat (prayer) immediately.
